question.text: A small spherical ball of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> falls freely under gravity through a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> will be ____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, viscosity of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>‐</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ).

solution.text:
Using equation of motion, v2=u2+2as

v2=0+2-g-h

⇒v2=2gh

Initial velocity of ball is v=2gh=20h.

 If after entering the water this velocity does not change, then this value should be equal to the terminal velocity.

Then, 2gh=29r2ρ-σgη, here, ρ is density of ball, σ is density of water and η is viscosity.

⇒20h=290.1×10-32104-103101×10-5⇒20h=2910-810-1103×101×10-5

⇒20h=400

∴h=20 m
